title: Effect of Alpha-S1-Casein Tryptic Hydrolysate and L-Theanine on Poor Sleep Quality: A Double Blind, Randomized Placebo-Controlled Crossover Trial

what_it_measured.text: The supplement or placebo was randomly and blindly assigned to 39 subjects for four weeks and the changes in the subjective sleep assessment via the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI), heart rate, blood pressure, salivary cortisol by high-performance liquid chromatography method and alpha power of awake electroencephalogram (EEG) were studied.
Psychological Measurement using PSQI The participants were required to fill out the PSQI [26], before and after the treatment of each stage.

dose.text: The supplement contained 150 mg CTH and 50 mg L-theanine in the same capsule while the placebo was a low-fat milk powder, encapsulated similar to the supplement.

route.text: The participants were instructed to orally take the capsules daily an hour before sleep and the compliance for study was checked verbally.

endpoint.text: Blood Pressure and Heart Rate Measurements Blood pressure and heart rate of the participants were measured by using the blood pressure monitor Microlife BP3AG1 (Microlife AG, Widnau, Switzerland) and an Omron Heart Scan HCG-801 (Omron Healthcare, Kyoto, Japan), respectively, before and after each treatment.
All the channels were used to calculate total alpha power while frontal alpha power was measured from the electrodes AF3, AF4, F3, F4, F7, F8, FC5, and FC6 and the average power was recorded.

reported_results.text: The supplement prolonged the total sleeping time by 45 min in the supplement receiving group compared to the placebo group (p < 0.001).

The latter depicted that RLX2™ improved PSQI total score, sleep latency, sleep duration, sleep habitual efficiency, daytime dysfunction, and increased total and frontal alpha power significantly (p < 0.05).
Although the placebo receiving group in Stage 1 showed a significant decrease in the PSQI total score by 1.38 (p = 0.026), this is likely caused by a placebo effect.
Based on the PSQI total score, supplement receiving groups had significant improvements (p < 0.001) compared to placebo in both stages.
A significant reduction of daytime dysfunction (component 7) was only observed in the supplement receiving group in Stage 2 (p < 0.001).
A significant placebo effect was noticeable only for the subjective sleep quality component (p = 0.037).
